column1: =每天一點，日積月累。這是一個陪你專注、推進長期計畫、照顧身心的練習空間。接下來用幾張卡片，帶你認識最重要的用法。
column2: A little every day adds up. This is a space to help you focus, move long projects forward and look after yourself. The next few cards show you the most important parts.

column1: =寫下今天最重要的三件事，按下番茄鐘開始專注。暫停時可以記下停在哪裡；冒出雜念就丟進「雜念停車場」。每段結束花十秒記下做了什麼，月曆和統計會自動累積。
column2: Write down today’s three most important things and start the Pomodoro timer. When you pause, note where you stopped; when a stray thought pops up, drop it in the “Distraction parking lot”. After each session, take ten seconds to log what you did — the calendar and stats add it up for you.

column2: “My rhythm” is a 12-minute questionnaire that finds your daily energy peak and dip and what motivates you most, then suggests a plan for your day. You can do it in parts — each part shows you its results right away.

column2: Plan practice by question type: which type today, which problem to solve, and how. Bring one type’s error rate down before moving to the next — you’ll feel progress every day. If a method doesn’t work, try another or talk it through with a teacher or classmates. Also check that your ID is still valid.

column2: Work through every question type once and find your problems: which type do you miss most, and why? Which takes the most time? No need for full mock exams yet — that’s for the last week.

column1: =列出未完成的項目，最模糊的先動一點，需要幫忙的早點開口。

column2: List what’s left and put it in order.

column2: When you’re stuck, ask a teacher or classmate.

column1: =固定作息，讓身體習慣考試的時段。
column2: Keep a fixed routine so your body gets used to the exam time.

column1: =好好休息，之後再回頭記下心得。
column2: Rest well, then come back and note what you learned.
Focus on the one thing that matters most.

column2: Bring your ID, eat something, breathe. Just show what you know.

column1: =帶齊證件，帶件外套。吃早餐、活動一下筋骨，先唸幾句幫自己暖身。考試只是把累積的展現出來，不是評斷你這個人。可以不完美，但不要輕易放棄。考完先好好吃一頓，再把題目回憶和表現記下來，之後檢討很有用。
column2: Bring your ID and a jacket. Eat breakfast, stretch, and say a few lines out loud to warm up. The exam just shows what you’ve built — it doesn’t judge who you are. It’s fine not to be perfect, but don’t give up easily. Afterwards, have a good meal, then note what you remember and how you did — it helps a lot when you review.

column2: Practice under exam-like conditions and keep a fixed routine. Review your process, not just the score.

column1: =用練習題或考古題找出最不穩的部分，優先補強。卡住時，向老師或同學求助。
column2: Use practice questions or past papers to find your shakiest parts and strengthen them first. When stuck, ask a teacher or classmate.

column1: =用練習題或考古題檢查自己，錯題就是線索。
column2: Check yourself with practice questions or past papers — every mistake is a clue.
Leave some buffer time for surprises.

column1: =確認時間、地點、交通和要帶的東西。
column2: Confirm the time, place, transport and what to bring.

column1: =確認送出成功，然後好好休息。
column2: Make sure it’s submitted, then rest well.

column1: =穩住步調，不要臨時大改方向。
column2: Keep a steady pace — don’t change direction at the last minute.

column1: =穩定的每日小進度，比偶爾熬夜更可靠。
column2: Small daily progress is more reliable than the occasional all-nighter.

column1: =穩定的每日練習，比偶爾一次的長時間更有用。
column2: Steady daily practice beats an occasional long session.

column1: =給自己的衝刺策略至少七天的時間好好執行。
column2: Give your final-stretch strategy at least seven days to work.
Nerves are normal — they mean you care.

column1: =考前三天不是翻盤期，確認流程就好。
column2: The last three days aren’t for turning things around — just confirm your process.

column1: =考完了，辛苦了！趁記憶還清楚，記下題目回憶和自己的表現。
column2: It’s over — well done! While it’s fresh, note what you remember and how you did.

column1: =記得確認報名、證件和考試資訊。
column2: Remember to check your registration, ID and exam details.

column1: =記得確認證件在考試前不會過期，現在換還來得及。
column2: Make sure your ID won’t expire before the exam — there’s still time to renew it.

column1: =證件帶好，早餐吃一點，放輕鬆。今天只是把你累積的展現出來。
column2: Bring your ID, eat some breakfast, relax. Today you’re just showing what you’ve built.

column1: =讓問題一個一個變少，比每天每科都碰一點更有效。
column2: Clearing problems one by one works better than touching every section a little each day.

column1: =辛苦了！先好好休息，再回頭記下這次的心得。
column2: Well done! Rest first, then come back and note what you learned.
How to prepare at this stage

column1: =選好日期，這裡會開始倒數，並每天給你一句提醒。
column2: Pick a date and this card starts counting down, with a reminder each day.

column1: =還不用急著做整份模考，先一個題型一個題型解決問題。
column2: No need for full mock exams yet — solve problems one question type at a time.

column1: =重做錯題時，重點是解題流程和時間，不是答案。
column2: When redoing mistakes, focus on your process and timing, not the answer.
Focus your review on what you got wrong.

column1: =開始收尾：整理、校對、確認格式。
column2: Start wrapping up: tidy, proofread, check formatting.

column1: =離截止還有時間，先把要做的事拆小。
column2: There’s still time before the deadline — break the work into small pieces first.

column1: =需要別人幫忙的部分，早點開口。
column2: Ask early for anything you need help with.

column1: =在「情緒覺察」或「覺察片段」記下情緒後，這裡會整理出常見的情緒。
column2: Once you log emotions in “Emotions” or “Moments”, your most common ones will appear here.

column1: =寫下每天最重要的三件事，這裡會看到完成的節奏。
column2: Write your three most important things each day to see your rhythm of getting them done.

column1: =數字是這段期間累計的強度（輕 1、中 2、強 3）。
column2: Numbers are total intensity over this period (mild 1, moderate 2, strong 3).

column1: =記錄兩天以上的身心分數，這裡會出現趨勢線。
column2: Log your scores for two or more days to see a trend line here.

column2: No meditation logged today yet. Finish a session and today’s notes will appear here.

column2: Saved automatically. Each session’s calm level, distractions and notes are gathered in the meditation section of “Stats”.
